title: Agent identity persistence across sessions
bottleneck: Agents have no stable, verifiable identity across sessions — no persistent memory of commitments, no continuity of principals, no reliable way for others to know they're talking to the same agent. Each session starts fresh, which breaks accountability, long-term contracts, and trust. Worse, the lack of identity infrastructure means malicious actors can trivially impersonate agents. Interaction dynamics are emergent and untestable in single-agent evals, so risks surface only in live deployments.
why_it_blocks: Economic and social roles require persistent identity. You can't hire, contract with, or hold accountable an entity that evaporates between conversations.
current_state: API keys and session tokens identify accounts, not agents. Production postmortems cite state corruption across sessions as endemic; no agent identity layer exists.
